litigation.note: The Board's Report discloses an Industrial Tribunal Award against the Company which it is challenging through Senior Counsel, on grounds including the Industry-cum-Region formula, the financial position of the Company and comparable industries not having been considered. The matter was simultaneously pending before the Labour Commissioner for execution of the Award, and on September 12, 2025 the Labour Commissioner ordered recovery from the Company; the Company is not admitting the liability and is in the process of challenging that Order before the Hon'ble High Court seeking appropriate relief. Separately, the Company has filed an appeal contending that Ministry of Finance Notification No. 32/2022-Customs (ADD) dated December 27, 2022, imposing anti-dumping duty on semi-finished lenses originating in or exported from China PR, provides insufficient remedy to the industry; that matter is awaiting pronouncement of Order. Read in the Board's / Directors' Report and the MD&A 'Opportunities and Threats' section.

risks.note: MD&A 'Opportunities and Threats' and the Board's Report both state the business faces stiff competition from China, with Chinese manufacturers dumping ophthalmic lenses in India at very low / below-cost prices. Management says this has created significant pressure on domestic pricing and margins and has resulted in reduced market share and lower sales realisation. The remedy the Company won - anti-dumping duty on semi-finished lenses from China PR under Notification No. 32/2022-Customs (ADD) dated December 27, 2022, effective for five years - is considered by the Company itself to provide insufficient remedy, and it has gone for an appeal, so the outcome is unresolved.
risks.risk: Import dumping from China at prices below cost

risks.note: MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' states that during the year the imposition of high tariffs by the US Government significantly impacted exports to the subsidiary Lensco - The Lens Company, New Jersey. The Board's Report adds that increased tariffs and trade restrictions imposed by the US government affected export competitiveness and demand in international markets. Recovery in FY2026-27 is explicitly conditioned on 'tariffs returning to normal levels', a variable outside the Company's control.
risks.risk: US tariff and trade-restriction exposure on exports

risks.note: The only risk management explicitly acknowledges in MD&A: 'We do not foresee any risks, except for foreign exchange fluctuations.' Because the Company depends on exports, the economic situation in exporting countries is stated as likely to affect performance - so both the currency and the destination-market cycle sit directly on results.
risks.risk: Foreign exchange fluctuation and dependence on export-country economies

risks.note: MD&A states the market remains heavily reliant on imported raw materials, with 65% of lens materials sourced internationally, and that this dependency, coupled with customs clearance delays and internal transportation challenges, continues to impact product availability across urban and rural regions. This compounds the forex exposure on the input side of the same P&L already exposed on the export side.
risks.risk: Imported raw-material dependence and supply-chain friction

risks.note: MD&A 'Segment wise or Product wise Performance' says only that the Company is engaged in the business of manufacturing semi-finished plastic lenses. There is no second product line or segment to absorb a shock in lens pricing or lens demand, so the China-dumping and US-tariff pressures hit the entire business at once.

MD&A states that domestic manufacturers face significant hurdles in expanding their business due to the dominance of international plastic lens manufacturers, and that growth of the local market is hampered by intense competition from low-cost imported lenses - a structural constraint on the very domestic-customer-base expansion the Company is relying on for recovery.
risks.risk: Scale disadvantage against dominant international lens manufacturers

risks.note: Under 'Significant and Material Orders Passed by the Regulators', the Board's Report discloses an Industrial Tribunal Panjim-Goa Award dated 25/05/2021 in Case no. 32/09 (Charter of Demands filed in 2009 by the Workmen represented by the Goa Trade & Commercial Workers' Union), which the Company is challenging by writ petition. On September 12, 2025 the Labour Commissioner ordered recovery from the Company for execution of that Award; the Company is not admitting the liability and is challenging the Order before the Hon'ble High Court. This is a live contingent claim in a labour-intensive business against a loss-making standalone entity.
risks.risk: Unresolved labour litigation and a Labour Commissioner recovery order

risks.note: Although the Auditors' Report is unmodified with no qualifications, reservations or adverse remarks, the Board responds to the auditors' Paragraph 2(b) observation that for records maintained by the inventory management software the electronic back-up of books and accounts is not being maintained on a daily basis. Remediation is stated as ongoing coordination between the concerned department and the technical team - a books-and-records control gap that remains open at the reporting date.
risks.risk: Internal-control observation on electronic back-up of books of account

- Product-technology advances - blue-light-blocking and anti-glare lenses, and high-refractive-index variants offering a thinner, lighter …

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The annual report discloses no new plant, greenfield project, brownfield line or capex programme with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Growth for FY2026-27 is planned entirely out of headroom in the existing facility: the MD&A Outlook states the Company has a normal capacity of producing 25,000 pieces of lenses per day against an installed capacity of manufacturing 35,000 lenses per day, and that having manufactured 34,88,865 pieces in the year ended March 31, 2026 it expects to increase this by 40% in the current financial year given demand, alongside a targeted sale of Rs. 36.00 Crores. …

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Long-tenured, stable workforce - of 156 permanent employees as on March 31, 2026, 140 have been with the Company for more than 10 years, with cordial labour relations and no interruption of manufacturing activities
- Established overseas route-to-market through wholly owned and step-down subsidiaries in Sharjah (UAE), Dubai and New Jersey (USA)
- Quality accreditation - ISO 9001:2015 from TUV SUD South Asia Private Limited
- 44-year operating history in the ophthalmic lens business (44th Annual Report), with capacity headroom - production is running below the stated installed capacity

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- MD&A 'Opportunities and Threats' and the Board's Report both state the business faces stiff competition from China, with Chinese manufacturers dumping ophthalmic lenses in India at very low / below-cost prices. Management says this has created significant pressure on domestic pricing and margins and has resulted in reduced market share and lower sales realisation. The remedy the Company won - anti-dumping duty on semi-finished lenses from China PR under Notification No. 32/2022-Customs (ADD) dated December 27, 2022, effective for five years - is considered by the Company itself to provide insufficient remedy, and it has gone for an appeal, so the outcome is unresolved.
- MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' states that during the year the imposition of high tariffs by the US Government significantly impacted exports to the subsidiary Lensco - The Lens Company, New Jersey. The Board's Report adds that increased tariffs and trade restrictions imposed by the US government affected export competitiveness and demand in international markets. Recovery in FY2026-27 is explicitly conditioned on 'tariffs returning to normal levels', a variable outside the Company's control.
- The only risk management explicitly acknowledges in MD&A: 'We do not foresee any risks, except for foreign exchange fluctuations.' Because the Company depends on exports, the economic situation in exporting countries is stated as likely to affect performance - so both the currency and the destination-market cycle sit directly on results.
- MD&A states the market remains heavily reliant on imported raw materials, with 65% of lens materials sourced internationally, and that this dependency, coupled with customs clearance delays and internal transportation challenges, continues to impact product availability across urban and rural regions. This compounds the forex exposure on the input side of the same P&L already exposed on the export side.
- MD&A 'Segment wise or Product wise Performance' says only that the Company is engaged in the business of manufacturing semi-finished plastic lenses. There is no second product line or segment to absorb a shock in lens pricing or lens demand, so the China-dumping and US-tariff pressures hit the entire business at once.
- MD&A states that domestic manufacturers face significant hurdles in expanding their business due to the dominance of international plastic lens manufacturers, and that growth of the local market is hampered by intense competition from low-cost imported lenses - a structural constraint on the very domestic-customer-base expansion the Company is relying on for recovery.
- Under 'Significant and Material Orders Passed by the Regulators', the Board's Report discloses an Industrial Tribunal Panjim-Goa Award dated 25/05/2021 in Case no. 32/09 (Charter of Demands filed in 2009 by the Workmen represented by the Goa Trade & Commercial Workers' Union), which the Company is challenging by writ petition. On September 12, 2025 the Labour Commissioner ordered recovery from the Company for execution of that Award; the Company is not admitting the liability and is challenging the Order before the Hon'ble High Court. This is a live contingent claim in a labour-intensive business against a loss-making standalone entity.
- Although the Auditors' Report is unmodified with no qualifications, reservations or adverse remarks, the Board responds to the auditors' Paragraph 2(b) observation that for records maintained by the inventory management software the electronic back-up of books and accounts is not being maintained on a daily basis. Remediation is stated as ongoing coordination between the concerned department and the technical team - a books-and-records control gap that remains open at the reporting date.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand the domestic customer base to offset weaker export demand and reduced market share
- Pursue the imposition of anti-dumping duties on plastic lens imports with the concerned authorities, having appealed on the ground that the existing Notification No. 32/2022-Customs (ADD) provides insufficient remedy to the industry
- Lift utilisation of the existing lens plant - production is targeted 40% higher in FY2026-27 against an installed capacity of 35,000 lenses per day versus a normal capacity of 25,000 per day
- Rationalise the overseas subsidiary structure - close the loss-making South African …

hero.oneLiner: GKB Ophthalmics is a Goa-based manufacturer of semi-finished plastic (organic) spectacle lens blanks with an installed capacity of 35,000 lenses per day, selling in India and through overseas subsidiaries in the UAE, USA and Africa.
